title: Client vs Server: Who Does What?
sources: Wikipedia, 'Client-server model': clients request a service or resource; servers host and share resources with many clients; communication is request-response
IONOS Digital Guide, 'How does the client server model work?': the client sends a request, the server processes it and returns a response; one server can serve many clients at once
AlgoMaster, 'Client-Server Architecture Explained': the client (browser, mobile app) shows the UI and sends requests; the server stores data, runs business logic and returns responses

lines.text: When you open an app, who does the work:
your phone, or a computer far away?
You're the guest at the table, so you're the client:
lines.caps: YOU'RE THE *GUEST | AT THE *TABLE | SO *YOU'RE | THE *CLIENT

lines.text: you read the menu and ask for what you want.
it keeps the ingredients, does the cooking,
and sends the dish back to your table.
sending a request like, show me my feed.
The server holds the photos and accounts,
does the heavy work, and sends back a response.
And one kitchen can feed thousands of tables.
